findings.claim: The declared objective is final predicted target affinity as primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; the reward view is the endpoint pointcloud with a detached Hungarian endpoint mean-squared-distance and native FLOWR endpoint VJP, so coordinate contrasts are reward-shaping signals rather than physical interaction energies.

The observed window is the score-time grid 0.00-0.49 with learning window [0.0,0.5] and curve support [0.0,0.49]; labels are recorded affinities removed under an equal score prior, so no absolute affinity target is observable and all coordinate statements are relative contrasts within this window.

Continuous contrast functions for landmark_00 features are non-monotone across the observed support: local_dy shows 6 sign changes with strong sign conflicts (first_rate_z -72.4, last_rate_z +5.5), local_dz shows 10 sign changes, and local_dx shows 6 sign changes with 9 strong sign conflicts; no polynomial fit is accepted and extrapolation is disallowed for any of them.

Whole-window z values for these landmark_00 features are small and mixed in sign (soft_mass +0.64, local_dx -0.18, local_dy -0.30, local_dz -0.02, local_cxx -0.58, local_cyy -0.58), so the endpoint-level marginal evidence does not support a stable signed direction for any single local coordinate descriptor.

Rate changes are large relative to level changes (e.g. local_dy first_rate_z -72.4 versus first_z +0.09; local_cyy first_rate_z -36.5 versus first_z +0.13), indicating that any time-conditioned contrast rule would be driven by within-window rate structure rather than by a constant offset; this is a diagnostic of the contrast curve, not a velocity force.

hypotheses.direction: time-conditioned rather than constant coordinate contrast
hypotheses.falsifier: If independent-batch agreement on the sign of the local_dy contrast at matched observed nodes is not better than chance, or if the sign-change pattern is not reproducible across batches, the time-conditioned direction is weakened and should not be used.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_local_dy and landmark_00_local_dz contrast values at observed score nodes
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned contrast on landmark_00 local_dy (and, secondarily, local_dz) may carry more usable signal than a constant rule, because the observed-node linear contrast changes sign repeatedly within the window while the whole-window mean is near zero.

hypotheses.direction: descriptive only; no signed marginal rule
hypotheses.falsifier: A reproducible same-sign whole-window effect across independent batches with a small number of sign changes would overturn this descriptive limitation.
hypotheses.observable: whole_window_z and sign_changes for landmark_00 soft_mass, local_cxx, local_cyy
hypotheses.statement: Isolated marginal landmark_00 descriptors (soft_mass, local_cxx, local_cyy) do not by themselves support a signed coordinate rule, because their whole-window z values are small and mixed in sign despite large first/last rate z values.

limitations: Only continuous_trends rows for landmark_00 features and the clocks/objective metadata were read; branch_adjusted, joint_diagnostics, regional_effects, increment_effects, turnover_accounting, survival_effects and endpoint_effects tables were not inspected, so multiplicity-adjusted support, independent-batch agreement, joint coupling and parent-child turnover could not be evaluated.
No absolute affinity target is observable: recorded affinities are removed and the score prior is equal, so all statements are relative coordinate contrasts within the observed window.

No registered reward recipe was selected or evaluated here; the permitted temporal_region recipe could express a time-conditioned contrast hypothesis, but this remains untested and no new reward is claimed.
The supplied evidence does not establish neural-module causation or physical interaction energies from these coordinate proxies.
